task.description:
WF-03 Step 4: write the regression test for ISS-0047 per the validated design's §5 (lib/letflow/design/iss-0047-username-race-conflict-target.md) -- a NEW, additive test using :auto sandbox mode with two genuinely independent Postgres connections (not :manual + Sandbox.allow/3, which cannot exercise this path -- see the existing REQ-018 race test at test/letflow/identity_test.exs lines ~259-355 for what NOT to reuse for this new test's mechanism, though its barrier-sync pattern can be reused for coordinating the two tasks). The test must provision two identical (external_realm, external_id) + identical preferred_username identities concurrently from two real independent connections, and prove both resolve to {:ok, ...} for the SAME user id (i.e. the race resolves cleanly via ISS-0047's fix), not an {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}. ISSUE-FIXER's own repro only reproduced the bug 4/6 runs (nondeterministic) -- the design's §5 notes this; structure the test to loop multiple attempts within one test (see design doc for exact guidance) so it's a reliable proof, not a flaky one-shot.

This is a WF-03 regression test: per WF-03_issue_resolving.md's Step 2-4 addition, you must show the test FAILS against the pre-fix code and PASSES against the post-fix code. Pre-fix commit is the one immediately before 548c338 on this branch (check git log). State this fail-then-pass verification explicitly in your handoff result, with actual command output from both states.
acceptance_criteria: New test added to test/letflow/identity_test.exs (or a new file if cleaner -- your judgment) using :auto sandbox mode with two real independent connections for the race itself.
Test loops enough race attempts to be a reliable proof given the 4/6 nondeterministic reproduction rate ISSUE-FIXER observed.
Test asserts both concurrent calls resolve to {:ok, ...} with the same underlying user id -- not an error.
Verified FAIL against pre-fix code (git stash or checkout the commit before 548c338), verified PASS against post-fix code -- both with actual quoted output.
Existing identity_test.exs suite (all other tests) still passes: MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs.

result.summary:
Added a new, additive describe block/test to test/letflow/identity_test.exs ("provision_oidc_user/4 — ISS-0047 regression: username-index race resolves cleanly", after the existing acceptance-criterion-3 race test, before the jit_config.enabled==false block). Test provisions one tenant schema, then loops 10 independent race attempts, each with a freshly-generated identity_context() (unique realm/external_id/username per attempt), racing two barrier-synchronized Task.async/1 calls to provision_oidc_user/4 under real :auto sandbox mode (two genuinely independent, automatically-checked-out Postgres connections -- provisioned_tenant!/0 already leaves the sandbox in :auto mode; this test deliberately does NOT switch to :manual+Sandbox.allow/3 the way the existing REQ-018 race test does, since that routes both Tasks through one shared connection and cannot expose this bug). Per attempt, asserts both results are {:ok, %{user: %User{id: _}, created: _}} (never {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}), same id on both, exactly one created: true, and exactly one row in the DB.

Fail-then-pass verification performed: found pre-fix commit 3d19e8c (immediately before 548c338 on this branch, confirmed by `git log --oneline -- lib/letflow/identity.ex`). Extracted `git show 3d19e8c:lib/letflow/identity.ex` to /tmp, diffed against HEAD's identity.ex to confirm the only difference is exactly the {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} branch + 3 new helper functions the design specifies (no unrelated drift). Temporarily copied the pre-fix content into lib/letflow/identity.ex, recompiled, and ran only the new test 3 times: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs:357` -> `31 tests, 1 failure, 30 excluded` on all 3 runs, with failure output showing `match (=) failed ... left: {:ok, %{user: %Letflow.Identity.User{id: id2}, ...}} right: {:error, #Ecto.Changeset<... errors: [username: {"has already been taken", [constraint: :unique, constraint_name: "users_username_index"]}] ...>}` -- exactly the ISS-0047 failure mode (username-index loser surfaces a raw changeset error instead of resolving cleanly). Restored the post-fix identity.ex (git diff confirmed zero diff against committed HEAD), recompiled, and ran the full file 3 times: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs` -> `31 tests, 0 failures` on all 3 runs, confirming both the new test and every pre-existing test (REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-063, the untouched genuine-collision test at former lines 379-394) still pass. lib/letflow/identity.ex was never left modified (git status confirms only test/letflow/identity_test.exs changed plus the new test/specs/ISS-0047.md spec file). Wrote test/specs/ISS-0047.md documenting the criterion, the test case, why it exists (existing race test structurally cannot exercise this bug), and the full fail/pass verification transcript.
